strings.en:
*High Councillor, this is the passage that I spoke of before. When we meet next, I would be happy to share the rest. I worry about circulating too much information unprotected, especially before our imminent departure.*     
  
After poring through Lenusso's journal, there are a handful of assumptions that I can make about traveling to the island of Castora:  
  
One. Based on various maps and documents that I've been able to uncover in Lion's Arch, I believe I've identified the correct landmass. It is to the far southwest, farther than most sailors have traveled. This aligns with various statements found throughout the source text.  
  
Two. It would be a deeply complex journey. While I suspect that it is about equal distance traveling from the Tyrian mainland to the Canthan continent, that stretch of ocean is highly treacherous. Most sailors that I consulted with have urged me to proceed with immense caution, if not drop the aspiration entirely. Not only did many refute the existence of such a place, but the general consensus is that modern vessels may not be enough to make it there intact.  
   
Three. Based on some of Lenusso's accounts, I am not entirely sure what to expect in terms of danger. There are hundreds of sketches of creatures I've never seen—references to incomprehensible magic! A dream to any researcher, explorer, or innovator...but perhaps more than I can conquer when the rest of the continent is focused on the rise of the White Mantle.   
   
Four. But I cannot ignore the possibility of what I may find on that island. While I can only guess based on the desperate musings of a now-deceased lab specimen, the picture that has been painted for me is one of intrigue and existential revelation. Imagine Rata Novus, which is already a spectacle of innovation, but better. No restrictions. Limitless power.

_Chapter 2_

Diah sighed wistfully. So many had swung by Jeb's farm over the years; they'd tend to some corn, stomp some wurms, and then move on. Most didn't even stop to talk. It made Diah feel small. Unimportant. Just a pit stop on a longer journey.

But this asura lad, Rollek? He'd introduced himself immediately, smiling the whole time. And as she watched him go about his tasks, she could feel his joy in the simple farm work.

"Fascinating, just *fascinating*." He muttered as he entertained one of her bovine, "Their reactions imply a high level of intelligence not supported by any current hypothesis..."

No one had ever complimented the cows before. Not even Jeb.

Hm. Maybe Rollek would appreciate a slice of her Tasty Cake.

"We used to train to hunt. Now we train to protect."
—Pact Crusader D'Stolt

strings.en: World Restructuring is in beta! Earn double WXP, increased reward-track progress, and increased magic find for the duration of the event!

While many of Gardesano's original tomes have been lost to time, I hope that with the right components we'll be able to craft new stewards. They may not be as elegant as the First Artificer's design, but perhaps we will see a bustling forge once more!    
  
**Step One**   
The forge's fabricators are functional but erratic due to age. They are spewing steward appendages in every direction. Artificers will need to catch these components and carry them to the appropriate workstation. For every new steward, you will need:  
1. Head  
2. Body  
3. Arms  
4. Legs  
  
**Step Two**   
Once the appendages have been assembled, you will need to combine them using a hammer.  
  
**Step Three**  
After assembly, carry the dormant steward to the Major Ley Infuser for attunement.  
  
Once enough stewards have been infused, we will begin a spell that will power them.  
  
—Leywright Edifi
